newsitem.title: POLAND: Hachette ignores new Ruch sale tender.
newsitem.headline: Hachette ignores new Ruch sale tender.

text.p: A consortium of French Hachette and Polish investors has ignored the Polish government's new invitation for bids for the country's largest newsstand chain Ruch SA, a Polish partner of the group said on Thursday.

Maciej Hoffman, head of Wydawcy Prasy firm, said the consortium considered its initial agreement on the sale of Ruch signed with the treasury ministry still valid even though the ministry had withdrawn from it.
"We do not accept that our rights to exclusive negotiations have been cancelled. (Treasury) Minister (Miroslaw) Pietrewicz violated the agreement signed in December 1996," Hoffman told Reuters.
"We wrote to minister Pietrewicz, saying that we uphold our offer from December and that we have no other proposals in this matter," he added.

In December last year the Hachette consortium and the ministry signed an initial agreement under which the group would buy a 75 percent stake in Ruch for a reported $84 million and raise Ruch's capital by another $45 million.

Last month the ministry annuled the agreement after a Polish group, which did not take part in the previous tender, said it was ready to pay more and the French-led consortium refused to improve its offer.
Therefore, the treasury ministry re-invited all interested investors to place bids Ruch, which owns 17,000 kiosks nation-wide and has a 65 percent share in the press distribution market in Poland.
The Polish group which challanged Hachette's offer is led by Universal and includes private television Polsat SA and soft drink producer and publisher Multico SA.
They have offered to pay $80 million for a 40-percent stake in Ruch and pledged to invest a total of $200 million in the company.
The sale of Ruch, which netted 16.2 million zlotys on sales of 2.7 billion zlotys in 1995, to Hachette was strongly advocated by French President Jacques Chirac during his visit to Poland last year.
